sonnet.problem: The statement says "by this we will know that we belong to the world" but never says what "this" is. The story card that explained it isn't on screen, so "this" points back to a card the baker can't see.
sonnet.rule: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

sonnet.problem: The question says "His commandment" and "His Son" without ever naming God. The baker can't tell who "His" is from this card alone.
sonnet.rule: "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.

sonnet.problem: The question and answers use "He" ("we know He remains in us", "He has given us") without naming God. Nothing in the card says who "He" is.
sonnet.rule: "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.

sonnet.problem: The text says "the love of God." The right answer turns it into "God's love," which takes a side on whether this is God's love or love for God. The text leaves that open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. / Call things what the text calls them.
